title: Adaptive Semantic Memory: Strong Project-State Results, Mixed Generalization to Long-Term Personal Memory
description:
Evaluation results, a standalone scoring script and a toy demo for ASM (Adaptive Semantic Memory), a compact state memory for long-running LLM agents. The ASM implementation itself is not included. Author: independent researcher, Ukraine (no institutional affiliation). Preliminary study, not independently reproduced.

EXP-001F, internal closed set c3 (built by the author; 12 synthetic scenarios, 216 questions per method, pre-registered, same Qwen3-235B-A22B reader): ASM v4.2 85.6%, full history 72.7%, BM25 56.5%, LLM summary 42.1%; ASM used about 12.6x less context (489 vs 6,164 tokens). Paired difference vs full history +13.0 pp (exact 95% CI +8.4 to +17.8).

EXP-002, LongMemEval ORACLE, 100-question stratified subset (public benchmark; not the official 500-question result; official GPT-4o judge): full history 66%, BM25 58%, ASM v4.2 49%, LLM summary 49%. ASM is weaker than BM25 (-9 pp, 95% CI -17 to -1, McNemar p = 0.064) and full history (-17 pp, p = 0.0015) on long-term personal memory.

Limitations: internal benchmark built by the author; one reader model; decision questions not clearly better (+2.8 pp, CI includes zero); false-update rate 20.5%; the c3 run is formally flagged for an API-accounting rule (audited: all questions graded).

Licenses: code in eval/ is MIT; data, report and README text are CC BY 4.0 (see LICENSE in the repository). LongMemEval data is not redistributed.
